key_insight: Mixed IQP-QCBMs stay locally trainable while gaining expressivity, but they only outperform ancilla-free IQP models when their branches separate into distinct modes.
engineering_relevance: For quantum generative modeling, cluster-aware initialization offers a practical way to speed up training and improve sample quality without triggering barren plateaus.
method: Define a mixed IQP-QCBM as a weighted ensemble of ancilla-free IQP branches.
Prove local barren-plateau avoidance for polynomially many branches under data-agnostic and some data-dependent initializations.
Use cluster initialization to assign different unsupervised data clusters to different branches and encourage mode separation.
evidence_signal: Exact 16-bit experiments and four benchmarks (binary clusters, 2D Ising, binarized MNIST, and a 484-spin glass) showed faster convergence and the lowest mean test MMD² for cluster initialization.
watch_item: Mode separation is difficult when branches start from nearly identical distributions, so performance depends on initialization quality and may suppress gradients needed to specialize branches.
paper_title: Trainability and Mode Separation of Mixed IQP-QCBMs
